A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 18-page paper, including complete appendices A1–A5. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original Max-Former classification experiments, ablations, energy estimates and runtime measurements in Tables 2–4 and 6–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Max-Former's 82.39% ImageNet top-1 accuracy in Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same Max-Former architecture: max-pooling patch embedding, early-stage depth-wise convolution, final-stage spiking self-attention and membrane shortcuts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification tasks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, CIFAR10-DVS and DVS128 Gesture. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the ANN and SNN baselines in Tables 2–3 and both QKFormer variants in the runtime and energy comparisons in Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: The model configurations, dataset splits, preprocessing, training budgets, resolutions, timesteps and evaluation procedures remain identical, including Tables 1 and 5 and the Appendix A3 timing protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the same patch-embedding and token-mixing ablations in Tables 4 and 6, shortcut analyses in Appendix A4, frequency visualizations and GradCAM examples.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for the benchmark comparisons. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, Max-Former retains 82.65% CIFAR-100 accuracy in Table 2 and 82.39% ImageNet accuracy in Table 3.

T1.justification: The neuron definitions, low-pass transfer-function derivations in Section 3.1, architectural equations and Appendix A2 energy formulas are unchanged. No assumptions or mathematical reasoning are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about network-level low-pass behavior, high-frequency information loss and Max-Former's accuracy and energy benefits.

C2.justification: The interpretations of frequency enhancement and shortcut tradeoffs remain unchanged. Appendix A4 retains the hardware-deployment qualifications, and Appendix A5 retains the limitation of manually balancing frequency components.

D1.justification: v2 adds 'Code is available' to the abstract, with a hyperlink to the project's GitHub repository. v1 only promises release upon acceptance in Appendix A1; that passage remains in v2. Implementation details, hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 57 numbered references and the discussion positioning the work against previous Spiking Transformers and frequency-based approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains the short code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording, section order and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Small text-formatting changes include the linked 'Code' text and newly bold 'A2' in Section 4's appendix reference. All seven figures and eight tables retain their content, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The new project-code hyperlink supplies an actionable access pointer absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. Appendix A1 still promises release upon acceptance, leaving inconsistent availability wording; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
